overview: This one-page Department of State list of papers, dated October 12, 1945, indexes five earlier items (sub-numbers 36–40) concerning Japanese iron, steel, and related manufacturing between June 1940 and April 1941. The entries point to reporting on Japan’s shortage of high-quality special steel, a Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce study of materials for the Japanese steel industry, a Justice Department memorandum on Japan’s iron and steel industry, transmitted articles on the industry, and a British Ministry of Economic Warfare memorandum on Japanese ball-bearing production. The page is an archival control sheet rather than the underlying reports themselves.

subfiles.summary: The sheet indexes documents numbered 36 through 40, dating from June 1940 to April 1941. Their subjects include Japan’s scarcity of good-quality special steel, a memorandum titled “New Material For The Japanese Steel Industry,” a Justice Department memorandum on the Japanese iron and steel industry, and articles transmitted to the United States in April 1941. It also records the transmission of a British Ministry of Economic Warfare memorandum on ball-bearing production in Japan; “Wall Bearing” in the OCR is evidently a misreading of “Ball Bearing.”

interest: The sheet is useful as a compact map of interdepartmental and Allied intelligence gathering about Japan’s strategic industrial capacity immediately before the Pacific War. It links naval reporting, the Departments of Commerce and Justice, and the British Ministry of Economic Warfare, showing how information about steel quality, material shortages, and bearing production circulated within the U.S. government. It also identifies several underlying reports whose texts are not present on this page and may therefore guide further archival research.
